stories.headline: BURYING ITS MANY DEAD; JOHNSTOWN NOW A CITY OF MORGUES. UNKNOWN BODIES HURRIED TO UNNAMED GRAVES. A CROWDED MORGUE. A TERRIBLE DEATH MILL.
REFORM IN THE BALLOT; CONNECTICUT'S EFFORT TO SECURE IT. HEARING BEFORE THE JUDICIARY COMMITTEE YESTERDAY--THE LONG CONTEST BE FOUGHT OVER.
stories.summary: HARTFORD,.--The interest in the Secret-Ballot bill attracted a large attendance at the bearing this afternoon before the Judiciary Committee. The principal supporters of the measure who were heard were the Hon. Henry C. Robinson and William A. Country man of this city, Speaker John H. Perry, the Rev. Dr. Chapin of Meriden, and Representative Wolff of New-Haven. Albert H. Walker of this city appeared in behalf of an envelope system.

stories.summary: LONDON, -- Young William's luck in politics has proved too good to last. All at once it has come to an abrupt and sensational end. Lifelong observers say there has been no such furious storm of partisan feeling in the Prussian Diet since the great battle over the army organization nearly thirty years ago as this which is now shaking Berlin.
